summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with morbid obesity, steroid-dependent psoriatic arthritis, insulin-dependent diabetes, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted from a rehabilitation facility due to recurrent episodes of hypoxemia, palpitations, and concern for pulmonary embolism. Initial evaluation ruled out new clots, but the patient had a subtherapeutic INR and a history of warfarin resistance. He was treated with heparin and carefully transitioned back to warfarin, with hematology input. Hypoxemia episodes were attributed to fluid overload and sleep apnea; he was diuresed from 386 to 366 lbs with improvement. A positive blood culture was deemed contaminated, and antibiotics were discontinued. His left leg wound showed signs of healing without active infection. A brief unresponsive episode prompted ICU evaluation and psychiatry consultation, resulting in a diagnosis of adjustment disorder with anxious features. The PICC line was removed due to safety concerns. Pain management was optimized with OxyContin and azathioprine restart. He was discharged home with services, on therapeutic anticoagulation, with follow-up arranged across multiple specialties.
